title: Normalized closed support and strict-limit comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite-field datum $D$, and a specified unit $\ell\in D.k$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be complementary closed and quasi-compact open immersions over $D.k$, with $X$ separated finite type and $Z,U$ finite type. Use the specified completed coefficient operations of [def-sf-integral-support-normalization-data] and their residue-field inverses. There is an ordinary integral comparison for $i$ whose actual reduction square is invertible. Ordinary module direct image is exact. The inverse of $\mathrm{closedAlpha}$ gives $d_i$ from the actual strict-system direct image to ordinary direct image, with the stated projection formula and actual finite reduction maps invertible. Ordinary direct image preserves derived completeness and every common reduction interval. The actual restricted closed direct image has its specified shift, agrees with $d_i$ and the universal-unit termwise comparison, and is exact. Its composite with actual open pullback is zero. These are precisely $\mathrm{ClosedSupport}$; this statement does not assert any open-extension comparison, either restricted adjunction, or any unit/counit restriction formula.

source.place: Triangle, Hom vanishing and constructibility paragraphs; the detailed integral normalization argument is the seven-step proof of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization, refined below.

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization] for the existing ordinary integral comparison closed, including its coefficient diagrams and normalized pull map. Its actual quotient counit gives closedReductionIso. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]: the quasi-compact open complement makes completed module closed image exact, giving finite limits and colimits preservation.

source.place: Integral support operations, detailed step 1 above, refining the corresponding part of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization.

proof.text: Let u_M be the actual quotient-tower completion unit. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], Koszul completeness is equivalent to invertibility of this unit. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] to closed image: its conclusion gives completeness of the image and the canonical direct-image/limit comparison. Scalar restriction and closed image both evaluate on the same fiber product, so they commute sectionwise and with all quotient transitions. Conjugating this strict reduction square by its specified adjunctions gives exactly closedLimit. Thus closedAlpha is the composite of ordinary image of u_M and that limit comparison. It is invertible on complete constructible inputs; its inverse defines di. Naturality and the finite projections give di_formula and closedProjection. The perfect projection formula in the cited comparison gives closedReductionComparison. The actual integral image here is the one of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Integral support operations, detailed step 2 above, refining the corresponding part of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization.

proof.text: For each finite reduction use [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] to write the input as inverse image of a bounded constructible etale complex. Exact site comparison [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] preserves its cohomological interval. A closed immersion is finite, so [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] compares closed derived image with etale closed image. The latter is exact and constructible by [lem-fin-closed-immersion]. Induction using truncation triangles identifies its cohomology with closed image of input cohomology. This preserves the same interval, including an empty interval. Together with the preceding completeness and reduction comparisons this proves closedInterval and closedComplete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

source.place: Integral support operations, detailed step 3 above, refining the corresponding part of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization.

proof.text: Closed image and scalar restriction act degreewise and commute with shifted differentials. In the normalized Roos model [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], actual augmentation has quotient maps as first component and zero second component. The limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] is the derived comparison of the underived sectionwise limit equality and commutes with these maps and the same cone signs. Therefore closedAlpha and its inverse di commute with the prescribed shifts. Restricting gives closedShiftInclusion; the exact-module right-derived/termwise comparison has this same shift because its defining universal unit is the termwise unit.

source.place: Integral support operations, detailed step 4 above, refining the corresponding part of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization.

proof.text: Exact ordinary closed image is triangulated with its termwise shift by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Restrict to the full integral constructible subcategories using [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] and the preceding preservation statements. The di shift equation transports this to the actual closed functor with the specified shift, proving closedExact. No restricted adjunction is part of this obligation.

source.place: Integral support operations, detailed step 5 above, refining the corresponding part of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization.

proof.text: The ringed open-closed zero identity of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] holds degreewise, since the relevant fiber product is empty. The normalized ordinary pull comparison in closed, invertible on complete inputs by its pull_complete property, identifies constructible pullback with ordinary restriction; di identifies the actual closed image with ordinary image. Transport the zero identity along these isomorphisms to prove disjoint. No open extension or open-support normalization is needed.
